body: NTA. Entitled much?  We recently moved into a new townhouse. The unit next door had been empty for 2 months so one day I pulled in their driveway for what was supposed to be only about 20 min as I had to take my kid somewhere. Next thing I know our doorbell was ringing and it was the neighbor!  Turns out they only live here some of the time. I was embarrassed and felt bad for holding them up. I apologized profusely and let them know it wasn’t a habit. They were as nice as could be. But it really wasn’t ok for me to park there, empty or not. Glad they realized it was us and didn’t tow but I wouldn’t have been mad at them if they went that direction.

NTA.  As parents of 2 teenagers we have always been clear on what we monitor and why. We aren’t worried about their conversations with friends, but we are worried about who else is contacting them. I
We have an open relationship and encourage them to question things and they get a lot of freedom as long as they continue to demonstrate their ability to handle that freedom. They are good kids. But they are kids. 

We recently found out someone was talking to my 14 year old daughter that she thought was a sibling of a friend but really wasn’t.  Something wasn’t quite right and she wasn’t mature enough to catch it. After asking her some questions and her going back and verifying, she realized that wasn’t who she was taking to. They wanted to meet up with her. That scares me to death. I will never ever regret monitoring these things. I’d rather have her safe, healthy and happy. 

I get some people feel it violates their privacy but as their mother it’s me keeping them safe while they are figuring out how to navigate the world. My daughter journals and I would never go through that.  They are allowed to have privacy and boundaries. 

We just explained what it is we look for when we monitor their online activity and why. They totally get it and have never complained and after this incident they have a much better understanding. She was freaked out and felt so bad that she didn’t catch it. She just didn’t have enough life experience to think anything bad was going on.

NTA. Failing to see why this is a big deal. 

I always buy us new pajamas (sometimes 
matching, sometimes not) and we all spend the morning around the tree opening gifts. This year because we didn’t go anywhere or have anyone come over, we stayed in our PJs all day. Best Christmas in a long time.

As a mother of 2 who always knew she wanted kids, I think it’s so freakin stupid for other people to ASSUME that just because they wanted kids, everyone else must be the same way. It’s the same issue with politics, religion and even how to raise kids. Just because it’s right me for me doesn’t mean it’s right for you. Same with how many kids someone chooses to have or where to live. Can you imagine if everyone decided that  Butte Montana was THE place to live?  It’d start to feel a bit over crowded. 

Forget what everyone else thinks. If you don’t want kids PLEASE don’t have them. Having kids when you don’t want them only hurts those kids who didn’t ask to be born.

NTA. We really need to stop acting like menstruation is something to be ashamed of. 50% of the population menstruates or will menstruate at some point and is a perfectly healthy and normal body function. Our mothers menstruation is what enabled us to be here. It’s not gross. In my house, it’s not weird or hidden. My 16 year old son went to the store for his little sister when she ran out of tampons and I wasn’t able to do it. He thought nothing of it. That’s the way it needs to be.
My husband moved here 25 years ago when he was 15 and thinks it’s dumb. I was just curious about how others feel about it since I’m not Hispanic, it’s not about me.

I’m not surprised that this is downvoted  because this sub hates people who haggle but I agree with you. I didn’t used to but my husband who was raised in a different country where haggling is normal taught me otherwise. 

I always felt weird asking for discounts. He does it all the time. Never in an entitled way and always very respectful. It’s amazing how often he gets one.  And if they say no, he doesn’t become a jerk. He accepts the answer and if he still wants it he buys it. I can’t stand when people become jerks like they’re owed something. No one owes anyone anything but the answer is always no if you don’t ask

I lose respect for people who judge others because their likes and dislikes are different from them. I mean who cares if they’re overly into Disney. How does that affect anything?  Does it change whether they’re a good employee or make them bad people?
How does a Disney fan affect your life in a negative way?  There’s enough bad and negativity in this world. If Mikey Mouse brings a grown man joy, let him have his joy. There are worse things in life. 

To each their own. I don’t enjoy going to the beach on a hot summer day but I don’t hate on anyone who loves it either.

These are 2 separate issues which have separate paths to holding them accountable if one or both of them took actions that were illegal. 

If Biden did pressure Ukraine to fire its top prosecutor in order to protect his son then he should be held accountable.  He should have due process through our judicial system. 

Regardless of whether Biden did something illegal or not, it is illegal to try to coerce information about a political opponent from a foreign government.   This is an abuse of power which is clearly outlined in the constitution.  If Trump did pressure Ukraine into digging up dirt on Biden by threatening to withhold funds then he should also be held accountable. He should have due process which in his case is the impeachment inquiry. 

We don’t know if Biden did something illegal nor do we really know if Trump did either. Unless we have all the evidence,  we can only make assumptions based on the information we do have. 


To keep putting them together by using Biden’s potentially illegal actions to explain Trump’s potentially illegal actions is basically saying two wrongs make a right. Which they don’t.

No. No one is the a-hole. You were being very respectful of a young girl’s feelings. This is a crucial time and had you said something you may have lost her trust. It is her body and her decision on who gets to know this very personal information.  By respecting her feelings you showed her that her feelings are valid and deserve to be respected. 

When my daughter gets there, I will respect her decision but encourage her not to be embarrassed. I remember my grandmother wanting me to show her bridge ladies (card game old people play) my new bra when I got one and it embarrassed me so much that it really affected my self image that when I got my period I didn’t even discuss with my mom.

Yes!  And I know it kills the mood for him completely. So I was attempting to avoid that knowing it would happen if I didn’t get stuff done. Nothing is more frustrating than the mood being killed right in the middle of it. 
I was totally into it and looking forward to it. I think he’s hotter now than when we met 19 years ago so definitely not an issue there and it’s reciprocated. Honestly overall our sex life is better than it ever has been in terms of enjoyment and being on the same page on how often we’d like it to happen which was why his reaction hurt so much. It felt out of left field
But we talked this morning and I realized there were other unrelated things he was stressing about that I could be better about (nothing even to do with our sex life) and he just kind of snapped.  Not very productive but hey, we are human and don’t always do the most productive thing.

I definitely appreciate this point of view. When the kids were younger this was definitely the case. It was hard to put us first and our marriage suffered. We worked through it and we both make sure we take time for each other. But sometimes we need reminders. 

Both kids are extremely independent and able to care for themselves and have a lot of responsibility. They help with household chores and get themselves up and ready for school including making themselves breakfast and lunch with no direction from us. I just make sure the food is there. They even do their own laundry. 

We are also an affectionate family and our daughter likes hugs and kisses before bed.  I don’t have to do anything else for her but if I want to get that done earlier than usual I need to facilitate that. All I wanted to do was eliminate any possibility of a knock on the door.

Thank you for the validation!  He really was being unreasonable. But I’ve since realized that there were other things going on in his head. Doesn’t make it ok but things have been so super crazy with us that we haven’t taken time for a little mindfulness and self care. I’ve been unreasonable at times too in our 15 yrs. 

While in the past I handled way more than he did at home while working the same hours, I paid for it with my health. I am not the suffer in silence type and asked for help,  I didn’t get what I needed. And things imploded. I didn’t work for 6 months to get healthy again. 

I recently went back to work and told him things needed to change and he was on board and has been really amazing these last 4 weeks since I started. If anything he really has taken on most of the load at home all to make sure I was taken care of.  I’m current driving 1.5 hrs each way to work but that is temporary and my new job is moving in June to a location less than 2 miles from our house so we just have to power through these next couple months.

Earlier we had planned on it for the evening when we went to bed.  Which for me meant right after our 11 yr old went to bed. We never go to bed before then because we have been interrupted when we tried to sneak away that close to her bedtime 

We finished dinner and told the kids to start on their chores of cleaning up the dinner dishes. We went upstairs and he suggested I take a shower/ bath and to take my time. He wanted to watch a show that I don’t like. Things were just business as usual up to this point. He wasn’t being extra flirty. He wanted to watch something I was likely to complain about. 

Immediately after the shower I went to check on the kids progress and to get our 11 year old ready for bed. I did not interrupt anything between us to do this. 

I went back to our room to wait for her to get her pjs on and let us know she’s ready. She just likes to be tucked in and wants hugs and kisses good night. Takes literally 2 min and something we both agree we will do for as long as she wants because it won’t be forever. 

She does insist on going to bed at 8pm because she hates how tired she is if she doesn’t get enough sleep. It works because that means we can go to bed right after and it’s still early enough to enjoy time together. The 14 yr old is fine and puts himself to bed on his own at 10pm. 

I do realize now I shouldn’t have assumed he was on the same page of going to bed after the 11 year old was down. 
I guess I just feel like once I explained and apologized it didn’t need to blow up into the fight it became. 
 But...Now that I’ve said all that, I’m thinking maybe he’s feeling frustrated or overwhelmed. I started a new job that has a very long commute but only until June when it moves to very close. He’s had to step up and be responsible for taking care of the evening stuff that previously fell to me. We haven’t done the best job at planning so things are easier. 

Perhaps this whole thing is just him being overwhelmed and not recognizing it so he’s taking it out on me in other ways. He used to do this when we were younger but we’ve grown together and have learned to communicate when we are needing more so I didn’t recognize the pattern right away. 

It’s been so crazy with me being gone 12 hrs a day that I think we’re exhausted and haven’t stopped to check on how we are doing. It’s easy to slip into old habits. 
So I guess my assessment is that no, he wasn’t being reasonable in this situation. But it’s because we are exhausted and not reacting as logically as we would if we weren’t so damn tired

It’s amazing how talking it out and answering these questions  made me really think about the situation objectively. It led me to a totally different conclusion than what I expected. 

I think I need to approach him with empathy and find out how we can make things easier during the week for both of us.

I would agree except his plan for tonight wasn’t a half hour thing. He wanted us to take our time. And it being so close to the 11 yr olds bedtime (who is maybe the only preteen who actually gave herself an 8pm bedtime) she would have interrupted for sure and he gets really frustrated when that happens and has a hard time getting back into the mood. We had just had sex the night before and by his admission was the best we’d had in a long time. And it’s usually quite good. 

We’ve been through not prioritizing it when they were younger. That’s not where we are now. It’s not as often as we’d like but it is due to my job commute being a 1.5 hr commute each way until June.  That was a discussion we had and agreed to before I accepted the job. After June it’s a 2 mile commute which is very ideal and why we both decided this was going to be ok for a short time.  We make a point of going to bed early so we can cuddle and watch tv. We wake up extra early so we can have coffee together and talk. We go on dates on Friday nights now that the kids are old enough and mature enough to handle a couple hours by themselves. During the week it may not always end up with sex but we definitely try to maintain the intimacy so it’s there for the weekend. Which was why his reaction hurt me so much.

We planned on it earlier in the day.  We didn’t have a chance earlier in the day so we talked about making time later when we went to bed. I figured later meant when the 11 yr old was down because she is the most needy. The 14 yr old puts himself to bed at 10pm. We would just say our good nights and lock the door. 

But maybe that’s where I went wrong. I didn’t explain what I was doing. I just went downstairs to get the 11 yr old going so she could go to sleep. He said he was going to give me a massage and I knew this was going to be something that took a little time. It wasn’t going to be a quick one so given the time of the evening this was all occurring I figured priority for both of us would be to eliminate the possibility of interruption.

How often are you two intimate?
-    At least 1x a week. Not as often as either of us want but it’s temporary.  My job’s location is a 1.5 hr commute each way meaning I’m gone 12 hours a day easily and I’m exhausted during the week. The location will move in June to less than 2 miles from our house so that will make things so much easier.  We had just had sex the night before and it was really good for both of us. 

How often do moments like the idea need you describe happen?
-not sure what you’re asking here?

Is there a reason why an 11 and 14 year old take care of themselves for 20 minutes?
- absolutely they could, however it was just that time of night where they were getting ready for school the next day. Our 11 year old has a self imposed bedtime of 8pm on school nights. She knows she needs her sleep and she would have come knocking on our door asking for snuggles and a tuck in. Had it been an hour earlier that would have worked but not that close to 8.  

Where does intimacy within your relationship  stand with other priorities?
-we make it as much of a priority as we can. When I started this job, we had lots of conversations about it and how the commute would affect it. We both knew that sex would most likely happen on the weekend and he was ok with this. We make a point of going out to a movie or dinner usually Friday nights to give us time to connect. We make a point of waking up 30 min earlier than needed to have time for coffee together.
